note: What a checklist item is CALLED when a homeowner reads it. Increment 4 Amendment 1 §C. The first twenty were named against a real gap list rather than chosen from the config — the reference export's twenty carried items — and ratified by the owner 2026-07-31.

ratification.note: Every name in `names` is ratified. A name that is not here yet may exist as an unratified proposal in the `client_names` table, written inline in the editor; this file wins over that table, and promoting a proposal means writing it here.
ratification.source: the twenty carried items on the reference export (housesteady-019f9a33), field config v1.2.1
ratification.scope: These twenty were named against a real gap list rather than chosen from the config. Nineteen are the ensuite's not-reached items; one is the close-out deferral. The int.* and wet.* entries come from the base interior and wet-room lists, so they recur in every room and every wet room respectively.
ratification.dateCorrection: 1.3.1 corrects the date only. 1.3.0 recorded 2026-07-30 for a ratification that happened on the 31st — a session handoff's date carried forward without being re-checked. No name changed; the version moved so two files with different hashes do not both claim 1.3.0. It is corrected rather than left because this one is a factual claim about a person and a day.

rules.note: The standard the next tranche is written against. A client-facing name is a NOUN PHRASE FOR THE THING. The sentence around it carries what we did or did not do.
rules.test: Does it read correctly inside the sentence the composer builds? 'We were not able to inspect under-sink plumbing' works. 'We were not able to inspect every sink cabinet opened and inspected while water runs' is the failure this exists to prevent.
prohibitions: No verbs of our activity — the item text is written for a concierge standing in a room, in the imperative. None of that survives.
No judgement words — suspect, defects, failures. House Style §3.
No internal vocabulary — pin as a verb, issue, zone types, item ids.
No instruction syntax — semicolons, slashes, parentheticals about how to capture.
No false precision — 'Under-sink plumbing' beats 'Under-sink supply and drain connections', which claims a scope the row may not have covered.

frames.note: How a group of carried items is introduced to a client. Reason first, then room — because 'we could not reach it', 'we did not get to it' and 'we have held it over' are different statements and must not interleave. The frame carries once for the group; the items are a list of names underneath it.
frames.status: RATIFIED 2026-07-31, with three corrections from the design session after the first render. See `corrections` for what changed and why — each one is a claim the earlier wording made that the data did not support.
frames.whyDeclaredRatherThanComposed: Twenty rows reading 'X — in ensuite — was not covered on this visit' is machine output, and House Style is what stands between us and that. Fixing it by generating a different sentence per row moves the problem; the frame has to be a written thing a person can read and change.

default.withRoom: In the {room}, we did not cover:
default.next: These are on the list for the next visit.
default.note: The default is the not-reached wording, because it is the claim that asserts least.

not-reached.withRoom: In the {room}, we did not cover:
not-reached.next: These are on the list for the next visit.

no-access.withRoom: In the {room}, we were not able to reach:
no-access.withoutRoom: We were not able to reach:
no-access.next: We will try again on the next visit.
no-access.note: The one reason the schema maps to `not-accessible`, and the only frame that may say we tried and were blocked, because it is the only one where that is true. A locked crawlspace is also the one distinction a homeowner can act on.

deferred.withRoom: In the {room}, we have held these over to the next visit:
deferred.withoutRoom: We have held these over to the next visit:
deferred.note: No closer, deliberately — see `corrections.deferredCloser`. And not 'you asked us to hold it': deferring may be our decision or the client's, and the record does not say which. House Style §7's rule about never claiming what we did not do runs in both directions.

frames.articleNote: The frames carry 'the' because the field app's room labels are bare nouns — ensuite, bedroom, garage. 'In ensuite, we were not able to cover' is what the first render produced and it reads wrong. A label that already carries an article would read 'In the the ensuite'; that is visible in the render, and nothing renders unsigned, so a person sees it before a client does.

corrections.notReachedWording: 'we were not able to cover' claimed we tried and were blocked. That is the NOT-ACCESSIBLE claim made over NOT-INSPECTED data — the exact asymmetry Amendment 1 §A3 exists to hold, arriving through the frame instead of through the label. 'we did not cover' is what the record supports.
corrections.noAccessMissing: There was no `no-access` frame at all, because the reference export produced nineteen not-reached and one deferred and the third reason never fired. A frame nobody wrote because nothing exercised it — the first locked crawlspace needs it, and it is the one place the blocked wording is finally true.
corrections.deferredCloser: 'No action is needed from you' dropped. A deferral can depend on the client — held until the well record turns up — and then it is false. The opener stands alone rather than guessing.

whyNotTheConfigText: Every one of this export's 266 items carries a `text` and NOT ONE of them is a name. They are checklist instructions written for the concierge standing in the room — 'Windows operated, locked, latched; seal-fog noted — pin defects'. Reading them as client-facing names does not withhold anything; it renders all of them. Four contain the word `issue`, which House Style §7 bans outright. Thirty-four use `pin` as a verb. Two carry markdown asterisks. Thirteen carry an em-dash the composer then wraps in more dashes. The measured version of the risk is in the PR that added this file.
howAnAbsenceBehaves: An item with no entry here is WITHHELD from the client render and reported as desk work, never rendered as its id. That is §2b's rule and it is now load-bearing rather than theoretical: today it withholds every row. The audit reports the withheld count beside the rendered one so the empty state is loud rather than invisible.
voice: A name, not an instruction. What the thing IS, from the homeowner's side of the kitchen table — 'The bathroom exhaust fan', not 'Exhaust fan runs, tissue test passed, termination traced to exterior'. House Style §10: no jargon without its plain-language twin at first use. House Style §7's banned words apply here as they do everywhere a client reads.
authorship: A human writes these and a human signs them. Doctrine 5 — AI may propose wording; nothing client-facing is AI-signed. §5's editor is where a concierge writes one inline for a row that needs it, and what they write lands here rather than on the property, because the name of a thing does not change between houses.

names.int.owner-quirks: Items you flagged in this room

notes.bth.fan-vs-window: Deliberately distinct from wet.fan. This one asks whether the room is adequately ventilated at all, which a window can satisfy. Both can appear in one list.
notes.int.alarms: Config text carries a parenthetical about photographing manufacture dates. An instruction about capture, not part of the name.
notes.int.canvas: About our record rather than their house — we did not get wide photographs of the room. Kept in because 'Missing from us' is exactly the column for things we owe.
notes.int.moisture-suspect: 'Suspect' dropped as a judgement word. The row's reason line carries the conditionality.
notes.int.owner-quirks: PROVISIONAL. Reads correctly when the owner flagged something and oddly when they did not. Watch it in the first real report — it may want the reason line doing more work, or it may be the first genuine case for the editor's inline override.
notes.int.receptacles: Config text ends 'pin failures as issues' — banned word plus internal verb in one string.
notes.int.windows: Config text ends 'pin defects' — same failure.
notes.wet.fan: Deliberately distinct from bth.fan-vs-window. This one is about the fan running and where it terminates.
notes.wet.surround-moisture: Paired with int.moisture-suspect; kept separable because one is a whole-room check and one is a specific surface.
notes.wet.under-sink: Config text carries literal markdown asterisks and a conditional instruction. Both dropped.
